label: D1 after a rare a2->S1 transition that was rewarded
explanation: Fires only at D1, never at GO or D2. About 83% of activation mass comes on D1 steps where the previous trial was the rare transition a2->S1 (it essentially never fires after the rare a1->S2 transition, and rarely after common ones). Most of the remaining mass is on the window first trial (rel -3), where the previous trial is not visible, so the same pattern is probably behind it. Within a2->S1 rare trials it is strongest when that trial was rewarded (the reward input is 1), which is exactly the case where a model-based agent should switch to a1. Adding the agent upcoming choice (action == 1, i.e. switching to a1) raises precision to 0.98, but recall drops to 0.25 (dev). So the top activations are D1 steps where the agent is about to switch a2->a1 after a rare rewarded S1 outcome. Weaker activations come on rare a2->S1 trials where the agent stays or the reward was 0. I recorded the predicate without the choice term: it uses only observed history and gives a better F1 (0.48 dev, mass recall 0.63). Precision is limited because many a2->S1 rare rewarded D1 steps where the agent goes on to stay with a2 stay silent.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=D1 & last=a2 S1 u (+3.53), phase=D1 & last=a2 S1 r (+3.42), phase=D1 & value_bin=decile 8 (9 = highest) (+2.72), phase=D1 & before=a2 S2 u (+2.48), phase=D1 & last=a1 S1 r (+2.05), prev_state=1 (+1.94). Lower it: phase=GO (-7.04), phase=D2 (-6.90), prev_state=2 (-4.38), choice_bin=decile 1 (9 = most a1) (-4.01).
